source: Benigni/Bossa rulebase for mutagenicity and carcinogenicity (a module of Toxtree)
citation: Benigni, R.; Bossa, C.; Jeliazkova, N. G.; Netzeva, T. I.; Worth, A. P. The Benigni/Bossa rulebase for mutagenicity and carcinogenicity - a module of Toxtree. JRC Technical Report EUR 23241 EN, European Commission - Joint Research Centre, 2008.
note: REBUILT 2026-09-01 after finding and fixing a real extraction bug: earlier passes over the full open-source Toxtree implementation (github.com/ideaconsult/toxtree-mirror, LGPL 2.1) were matching SMARTS text inside Java /* */ comment blocks (dead/superseded code, or hand-written documentation of what a programmatic pattern produces) as if it were the live addSubstructure() call -- confirmed by direct manual inspection of the comment-stripped source for SA2/SA8/SA25/SA27/SA28, which either have NO literal SMARTS in their real (StringBuffer-built) logic at all, or (SA28) only 2 minor fragment patterns while the real core 'primary aromatic amine' logic is built programmatically and was never captured. Final extraction methodology (scripts referenced only in this repo's own scratch history, not checked in): (1) strip Java comments FIRST; (2) find every addSubstructure(name, value) call; (3) if value is a bare identifier (not a literal string), resolve it to the LAST `String X = "literal";` assignment to that EXACT identifier appearing before that specific call (handles variable shadowing correctly -- an earlier attempt used a single global name->value dict and silently picked up a similarly-named-but-wrong variable for SA10); (4) every resulting SMARTS compiled in RDKit; (5) cross-checked against the rule's own embedded example SMILES (examples[0]/examples[1] in the Java source, typically a negative-control/positive-example pair) via RDKit substructure matching on an explicit-H graph. 13 rules from the full Toxtree ruleset (SA_4, SA_10, SA_11, SA_15, SA_17, SA_30, SA_31b, SA_31c, SA_42, SA_44, SA_47, SA_49, SA_50) passed every check and are included below alongside the original 9 from Ferrari & Gini 2010's supplementary material (SA_1, SA_6, SA_7, SA_12, SA_13, SA_14, SA_16, SA_21, SA_22 -- a different, independent source, unaffected by this Java-comment bug) and the 2 custom-code ring-fusion alerts (SA_18/SA_19). Explicitly EXCLUDED and why: SA_2, SA_8, SA_25, SA_27 (no literal SMARTS exists anywhere in the live code -- fully built via StringBuffer/loops over substituent tables); SA_28 (only 2 minor fragment patterns are literal, the real core logic is programmatic -- shipping just the fragments would misrepresent the alert); SA_23, SA_24, SA_29 (own example SMILES use a non-standard nitro-group notation RDKit can't parse, so correctness could not be verified); SA_48 (its own stated positive example does not match the extracted pattern); SA_43/SA_45/SA_46/SA_51 (fewer than 5 positive occurrences across the 6505-molecule Ames dataset, numerically risky for descriptor scaling and no real signal). Every SMARTS below has now been independently confirmed correct by hand against the live, comment-stripped Toxtree source, not just by a script's own self-report.
